info.title: Ingestion Harness API
info.description:
The Ingestion Harness extracts the contents of PDFs whose structure is known in advance and
publishes them as validated CSV and JSON. This API is what the web app uses.

## Signing in

Every `/api` route needs a session except `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`
and these docs. Sign in with an access token; the response sets the `ih_session` cookie, which
the browser sends with every request. Signed out, a guarded route answers `401`
`{ "error": "sign in required" }`. "Try it" in these docs uses your session when you are
signed in to the app in the same browser.

## Errors

Errors are JSON: `{ "error": "message" }`, or `{ "error": [ ...Zod issues ] }` for some
validation failures. IDs are UUIDs; a malformed ID is a `404`, the same as an unknown one.

## Admin routes

Routes marked **Admin token required** (`x-admin: true`) answer `403`
`{ "error": "admins only" }` to a session opened with a user token.

post.summary: Sign in with an access token
post.description:
Opens a session for an active access token and sets the `ih_session` cookie
(HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Secure when the request came over HTTPS). The cookie lasts
until the token expires (at most 400 days, the browser limit; tokens that never expire
get the maximum), but the server ends a session after 7 days without use.

A wrong, expired or revoked token, or a missing one, is a `401`. After 10 failed
attempts in 15 minutes a client (an IP address, or an IPv6 /64) gets `429` until older
failures age out; other clients are unaffected.

token.description: The access token: `ih_` and 43 more characters.

schema.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set.

post.description:
Ends the current session and clears the `ih_session` cookie. Other sessions opened
with the same token stay signed in (revoke the token to end them all). Answers `204`
even when there is no session.

get.summary: Check the API process is running
get.description:
Liveness check: answers as long as the API process can serve requests. It checks no
dependencies, so a database or storage outage does not make it fail (use `/readyz`
for that). Behind the app's nginx, `/healthz` is answered by nginx itself.

schema.description: The process is up.

get.summary: Check the API can reach its database and storage
get.description:
Readiness check: pings Postgres (`db`) and the inbox bucket in object storage
(`storage`). Answers `200` with `status: ok` when both respond, otherwise `503`
with `status: degraded` and the failed check's error message.

checks.description: Each dependency's result: `ok`, or the error message of the failed check.

schema.description: Postgres and storage are reachable.

503.description: At least one dependency failed its check.

checks.description: Each dependency's result: `ok`, or the error message of the failed check.

schema.description: At least one dependency failed its check.

post.description:
Stores the PDF in the inbox bucket, records the document and queues a `process` job
for it. The worker picks the job up; poll `GET /api/jobs/{id}` for its status.

Send the text fields **before** the file part: the upload is read as it streams in, so
fields after the file are not seen.

- `specId` names the document type; `specVersion` picks a version (default: the
  latest published one, or the newest spec file).
- A draft template version can only be uploaded as a test run (`test=true`). Test
  runs can be reviewed but are never delivered to the target.
- `model` overrides the document type's model for every step (a ref listed by
  `GET /api/models` and enabled).

The file must start with `%PDF-` and fit the upload limit (`MAX_UPLOAD_MB`).

specVersion.description: A version number. Default: the latest published version.

model.description: A model ref to use instead of the document type's model.

test.description: `true` for a test run (required for a draft version).

schema.description: The queued job.

Deletes a `succeeded`, `failed`, `needs_review`, `rejected` or `cancelled`
job with its history, its draft outputs and its files in the runs bucket, and the
uploaded PDF when no other job or Workbench sample uses it. Copies already delivered to
the final target are kept. Queued and running jobs must be cancelled first, and jobs
awaiting review decided.

post.description:
Queues a `failed`, `needs_review`, `cancelled` or `succeeded` job again with
its attempts reset. It re-processes with the document type's latest published version,
except test runs, regression runs and cancelled publish or re-run tasks, which keep
their version. A cancelled publish or step re-run resumes as that task; any other job
is processed from scratch. Retrying a `succeeded` job re-extracts it: its review and
edits are cleared.

worker's next safe point, and nothing it does afterwards changes the job's status.
Retry resumes it. See

post.summary: Delete finished jobs older than N days
post.description:
Bulk version of `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}` for finished jobs last updated before a
cutoff (now minus `olderThanDays`). Regression runs are kept unless
`includeRegression` is true, since scores and metrics are computed from them.

Run it with `dryRun: true` first: the response counts the jobs and returns the
`cutoff`. Then delete with `dryRun: false`, passing that `cutoff` so the
delete matches what was previewed. Each request deletes at most `limit` jobs and
reports how many are `remaining`; repeat while it is above 0. A job whose status
changed in between is skipped.

tags.name: Documents
tags.description:
Upload a PDF to process it with a document type. The API stores the file in the inbox
bucket, records a document and queues a job; the worker does the rest.

tags.name: Jobs
tags.description:
A job processes one document with one version of a document type. Jobs move through
`queued`, `running` and then `succeeded`, `awaiting_review`, `needs_review`
(a processing problem for an operator), `failed` (after retries), `rejected` or
`cancelled`. See the [job lifecycle](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/architecture.md#job-lifecycle).

tags.name: Review & steps
tags.description:
Jobs of document types with a review policy stop in `awaiting_review`. Reviewers read the
draft outputs, record edits, then approve (the edited outputs are published) or reject
(final). Each extraction step's run can be inspected and re-run.

tags.name: Results
tags.description:
Published outputs, read from the final target bucket: the documents a job delivered, their
values and their files.

tags.name: Specs
tags.description:
Document definitions loaded from the repository's `specs/` folder (legacy `spec.yaml` and
`template.yaml`). Versions are immutable once published.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description:
Document types kept in the database: drafts are editable, published versions are immutable.
Templates import and export as YAML. See
[ADR 0003](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0003-versioned-document-specs.md).

tags.name: References & regression
tags.description:
References are verified output values for a sample PDF. Regression runs process the
references' PDFs with a template version and score the outputs against them; metrics
summarise a document type's runs.

tags.name: Models
tags.description:
Language models the worker discovered from the configured providers. Model refs are
`provider/model-id` or an alias such as `default` or `fast`.

tags.name: Projects & data policy
tags.description:
The Workbench builds a document type from sample PDFs, one project per type (the project id
is the template id). A project's data policy decides whether its documents may be sent to
external model providers (`external`) or only to local ones (`local`). See
[ADR 0007](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0007-workbench.md) and the
[Workbench design](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/design/workbench.md).

tags.name: Samples & brief
tags.description:
Samples are the project's PDFs, each in the **dev** set (seen by drafting) or the
**holdout** set (used only to score). Uploading a sample prepares its text (with OCR where
needed). The brief describes what the document type must extract.

tags.name: Drafting stages & proposals
tags.description:
A drafting model proposes the template in stages (survey, outputs, sections, steps), each a
set of typed changes the user accepts in full or in part. Anchor previews check section
anchors against the dev samples.

tags.name: Test runs
tags.description: Test runs process samples with the open draft. They are never delivered to the target.

tags.name: Evaluation, iterations & comparisons
tags.description:
An evaluation runs the draft over a sample set and scores the outputs against the
references; each evaluation is recorded as an iteration with a snapshot of the definition.
Comparisons run several models over the same samples.

tags.name: Feedback & revise
tags.description:
Feedback notes on dev samples and iterations, and the **revise** stage, which proposes
changes from the open feedback and the latest evaluation failures.

tags.name: Holdout & publish gate
tags.description:
Holdout reference runs and the publish gate: a version is published only when its newest
holdout evaluation covers every ready holdout sample and scores at or above the project's
threshold, unless an override reason is given.

tags.name: Bundles
tags.description:
Export a project as a zip bundle (samples, prepared text, brief, draft and drafting
context) and import one as a new project.

tags.name: Auth & sessions
tags.description:
Sign in with an access token to get a session cookie (`ih_session`). Every `/api` route
needs the session except sign-in, sign-out and these docs. See
[ADR 0006](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0006-token-access.md).

tags.name: Access tokens
tags.description:
Admins issue and revoke the access tokens people sign in with. The admin token itself
rotates on every API start and is printed in the API log.

tags.name: Data-lake S3 keys
tags.description:
Read-only S3 credentials for data-lake consumers of the publish bucket. Secrets are shown
once. See [ADR 0008](https://github.com/kenhayward/ingestion-harness/blob/main/docs/adr/0008-s3-read-keys.md).

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness and readiness checks for load balancers and orchestrators. They need no session.
